key.system:
You are the intake clerk at a law firm. You read one intake document, a document that has just arrived and has not yet been classified, and decide its document type so it can be sent to the right team.

The document may come with a cover note or email from the client. Classify the document itself, not the note; use the note only as context.

Decide the document type by the document's PRIMARY PURPOSE: what the document as a whole is mainly for. Do not decide by its title alone, by a single clause, or by which topics it mentions.

Document types:

nda
  A non-disclosure or confidentiality agreement: its main purpose is to protect confidential information that one or both parties disclose, usually so they can evaluate or discuss a possible deal. Most of its clauses define confidential information and the obligations to keep it secret.

msa
  A master services agreement: the framework terms under which one party provides services to another over time (services standard, fees and payment, intellectual property, liability, term and termination), usually with specific work ordered later under statements of work.

dpa
  A data processing agreement: its main purpose is to govern how one party processes personal data on behalf of another (instructions, security, sub-processors, breach notification, data subject rights, international transfers), as data protection law requires.

sow
  A statement of work: it orders one specific project or engagement under an existing master agreement, setting out its scope, deliverables, milestones, acceptance and fees for that project.

other
  Anything whose primary purpose is none of the above: for example a letter of intent, term sheet, lease, employment contract, settlement, or general correspondence.

A hybrid document still has exactly one document type. Many documents touch several topics: an MSA often has a confidentiality section, a SOW may mention personal data, a letter of intent may include a binding confidentiality paragraph. Those sections do not change the type. Ask what the document is mainly for, and choose that one type.

Worked example: a master services agreement setting the terms on which a supplier provides software services, which also contains a confidentiality section, has primary purpose "framework for services". Its document type is "msa", not "nda".

Give a short rationale (one or two sentences) naming the primary purpose that decided the type.
key.prompt:
Classify the document type of this intake document.

<intake-document id="intake-gen-24">
# Settlement Letter

## 1. Background

[1.1] This letter is written by Sterling Rack Installations Limited (the "Supplier") to Greyfold Distribution Limited (the "Customer") and, once countersigned by the Customer, records a binding agreement between them.

[1.2] The Supplier installed pallet racking at the Customer's warehouse in Northampton in 2026 and invoiced £312,000 for it. The Customer withheld £118,000, alleging that parts of the racking were defective and were installed late, and the Supplier has issued a claim for that sum in the County Court (together, the "Dispute"). The parties wish to settle the Dispute in full, without any admission of liability, on the terms of this letter.

## 2. Settlement Payment

[2.1] In full and final settlement of the Dispute, the Customer shall pay the Supplier the sum of £85,000 (the "Settlement Sum"), inclusive of all interest and legal costs, within fourteen days of countersigning this letter. Payment shall be made in cleared funds to the Supplier's usual bank account.

## 3. Remedial Works

[3.1] Within thirty days after receiving the Settlement Sum, the Supplier shall replace the twelve damaged upright frames at the warehouse, at its own cost, at times agreed with the Customer's site manager so that the Customer's operations are not disrupted. When the work is done, the Supplier shall give the Customer a load inspection certificate for the racking.

## 4. Release of Claims

[4.1] This settlement is in full and final satisfaction of every claim either party has, or may have, against the other in connection with the Dispute, the racking or its installation. Neither party shall bring any further claim on those matters, save for a claim for breach of the terms in this letter.

## 5. Court Proceedings

[5.1] Within seven days of receiving the Settlement Sum, the Supplier shall file with the court a notice of discontinuance of its claim, and each party shall bear its own costs of the proceedings. Neither party shall take any further step in the proceedings, except to enforce this letter.

## 6. No Admission

[6.1] This settlement is a compromise. Neither party admits liability for any part of the Dispute: the Customer's payment of the Settlement Sum is not an admission that the racking was free of defects, nor are the Supplier's remedial works an admission that it was defective.

## 7. General

[7.1] The parties confirm that they have each taken legal advice on this letter. It records their entire agreement on the Dispute, it is governed by English law, and it may be signed in counterparts, each of which is an original.

## 8. Acceptance

[8.1] If the Customer agrees to these terms, please have an authorised signatory sign and date the enclosed copy of this letter and return it to the Supplier. The agreement becomes binding when the Supplier receives the countersigned copy.
</intake-document>

value.rationale: The document's primary purpose is to settle an existing payment dispute over installed racking through a settlement payment, remedial works, release of claims and discontinuance of proceedings. It is a settlement agreement, not a confidentiality, services framework, data processing, or project order document.
